page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-96 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n1 server family. It features 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor using x86_64 architecture with Hyper-Threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 360 GB of dedicated RAM, providing a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 3.75 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate a clear dichotomy between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, scoring in the bottom 25% for stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tasks. However, the high core count enables strong multi-core performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with cached and uncached read-only operations, as well as uncached write operations, ranking in the top 25%. Database operations and static web serving throughput perform in the average tier, while Redis SET operations demonstrate strong throughput. Large language model inference shows average prompt processing speeds but poor text generation performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-96 offers a dense allocation of Intel Xeon resources suited for highly parallelized workloads that can offset the lower single-core efficiency. The lack of local storage and GPUs makes it less suitable for direct high-speed storage-bound databases or hardware-accelerated machine learning training. Instead, it is best suited for multi-threaded general-purpose workloads, such as parallel software compilation, medium-scale database operations, memory-cached web serving, and batch processing tasks that benefit from high memory bandwidth and high core counts.
